e: Peru cuts diplomatic relations with Iran, accusing Tehran of escalating the 2026 Iran war and citing a historic pacifist stance.
Four people are sentenced to up to 35 years' imprisonment for the 2023 murder of indigenous environmental activist Quinto Inuma Alvarado.
A magnitude 6.7 earthquake hits Ayacucho Department, injuring three people.
A minibus collides with a truck in Espinar Province, Cuzco Department, killing 13 people.
A magnitude 4.4 earthquake hits Junín Department, killing one person.
A magnitude 5.0 earthquake hits Junín Department, injuring 12 people.
A Cessna 208 Caravan carrying tourists to view the Nazca Lines crashes near Socos, killing 11 passengers and two pilots.
Luis Galarreta is appointed prime minister.
Keiko Fujimori is sworn in as president, succeeding José María Balcázar.
A collision between two buses in Tacna kills five people and injures 16 others.
The United States imposes a 12.5% tariff on Peru, citing the presence of alleged forced labor in the supply chain.
Ten members of the same family, including five children, are killed in a house fire in the La Victoria District of Lima.
A magnitude 5.5 earthquake hits Junín Department, killing five people and injuring 71 others.
A bus overturns in Huánuco Department, killing 11 people and injuring 15 others.
A magnitude 5.8 earthquake hits Ica Department, injuring 27 people.
A minibus collides with a fuel truck in Cerillos, Department of Puno, killing seven people.
A tourist bus plunges into a ravine in Huarochirí Province, killing 10 people and injuring 15.
A minibus collides with a truck in Caylloma Province, killing 13 people.
Denisse Miralles resigns as prime minister before a confirmatory vote could be taken in Congress. She is replaced by Luis Arroyo Sánchez.
At least 44 people are injured in a bombing at a nightclub in Trujillo, La Libertad Department. Three people are arrested the next day.

The Inter-American Court of Human Rights holds the Peruvian state responsible for the 1997 death of a woman who died from the forced sterilization program of president Alberto Fujimori and orders it to pay $340,000 in compensation to the victim's heirs.
A state of emergency is declared in more than 700 districts nationwide due to flooding and landslides.
Denisse Miralles is inaugurated as prime minister.
Hernando de Soto is announced as the new Prime Minister of Peru. Later that day, de Soto declines the appointment.
Two people are killed in a landslide in Arequipa.
A Mil Mi-17 helicopter of the Peruvian Air Force crashes in Chala Viejo, Chala District, killing all 15 people on board.
Congress elects José María Balcázar as interim president.
Congress removes President José Jerí from office for failing to disclose meetings with Chinese businessmen.
